einstellungen.text: Tomorrow, your apartment gets taken apart. You can bring one box.
One box per person. The dome doesn't have more room.
Your space station needs empty rooms to survive. Now it's your turn.
You pick something up. Put it down. Pick it up again.
Forty-three of your drawings. Your first space suit patch. The mug with the crack.
Bo is done in five minutes. He's got his tape. That's all he wants.
Your mom packs only tools. Like she's practiced saying goodbye.
At midnight you sit alone at the kitchen table. Rough scratches under your fingers.
You carved those when you were six. Your mom yelled, and then she laughed.
Your mom sits down next to you. She brings two mugs of tea.
"I want to keep everything too. Every single thing."
You talk for two hours. Longer than you have in months.
Afterward, you go check on Bo. Since his room's been gone, he sleeps in yours.
Bo is asleep. Under your bed there's a print in the dust. A clean rectangle.
A box of Bo's was sitting there. One you've never seen. And now it's gone.
